q: Why is ROAS increasing while net profit is declining?

checks.what: tool: ROAS attempted or derived from its definition

answer:
Net ROAS has risen because ad spend fell much faster than contribution margin; net profit, however, did not decline — it improved (loss narrowed) over the same comparison. 

Evidence (measured)
- Net ROAS (order-date): 0.74 → 0.97 (period 2026-08-16..2026-09-13 → 2026-09-15..2026-10-13) — Net ROAS +31%. 【Measured】
- Net profit (order-date): ₹-532,557 → ₹-28,490 (same periods) — loss reduced (net profit improved). 【Measured】

Why (measured drivers and accounting)
- Ad spend dropped far more than contribution margin:
  - Ad spend: ₹2,069,132 → ₹1,002,451 (−52%) — this alone moved Net ROAS up by ~+0.65x and improved net profit (ad spend is subtracted in profit). 【Measured】
  - Contribution margin: ₹1,536,575 → ₹973,961 (−37%) — this pulled Net ROAS down by ~−0.42x and reduced profit. 【Measured】
- Net effect on Net ROAS: ad spend ↓ > contribution margin ↓ → overall Net ROAS up (arithmetic split above). 【Measured / arithmetic】
- Net profit improved because the reduction in ad spend (a direct subtraction from profit) outweighed the drop in contribution margin, so the net loss narrowed. The catalogued identity net profit = contribution margin − ad spend holds exactly for the periods. 【Measured / accounting identity】

Quick channel note (measured)
- Both Meta and Google saw big ad‑spend cuts and lower contribution margin; Meta contributed most to the net-profit improvement because its ad spend decline was the largest in absolute INR. 【Measured】

Context: Period: 2026-09-15..2026-10-13 vs 2026-08-16..2026-09-13 · Currency: INR · Data as of 2026-10-14.
